answer: Every identity must lock a deposit in a shared vault, and each epoch a random jury of unrelated agents may challenge any vertex in the trust graph. If the jury proves the identity is a duplicate, its vault deposit is slashed and paid to the challengers. A single sparrow of an honest agent risks one deposit and passes easily, while a farmer must fund thousands of deposits and loses them all once one fake cluster is exposed, making forgery more expensive than honest work.
